newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy must look to structural spending cuts - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italy must look to structural spending cuts - Fazio.

text.p: The government should concentrate its budget efforts on structural spending cuts, Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Thursday, adding that this would favour monetary easing.

"In our country, budgetary adjustments should continue by concentrating efforts on the spending side, aiming at structural reforms which would guarantee a long term re-balancing (of state accounts), favouring a fall in the cost of money," Fazio said in a speech to mark the world day of savings.
"This is necessary for full participation in the process of the integration and construction of a united Europe," he added.
The government last month unveiled a 62.5 trillion lire budget, designed to win Italy a place in the first wave of countries into planned European economic and monetary union.

Much of the budget is built around new revenue-raising schemes and employers' federations have criticised the government for largely avoiding a structural overhaul of welfare spending. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
